text:
In August of 2013, thirty-five of us arrived at the same seven words: "keep the irs off your." Thirty-five said "irs off your health care." John Cornyn said it first, on 2013-05-16, and by 2013-08-02 we had converged on it together. Thirty-four of us carried "keep the irs off your health" and "the irs off your health care" the same day. Thirty-three of us added "irs off your health care act."

Beneath that, a second line ran through us. Thirty-one said "in need of scrutiny"; thirty of us said "regulations from the executive in need" and "the executive in need of scrutiny." Tim Walberg said it first, on 2013-01-25, and we caught up to him by 2013-08-02.

We record only that these were the phrases we repeated, and how many of us repeated each.

top_phrases.phrase: keep the irs off your health
the irs off your health care
irs off your health care act
regulations from the executive in need
the executive in need of scrutiny
